chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever swears an oath, then sees other than it to be better than it, and does that — then it is the expiation for his oath, and for him is a reward.

key_terms.حَسَنَة: Good deed/reward (hasana); a merit recorded in one's account with God for choosing the better course
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation (kaffara); an act of atonement that removes the sin or obligation attached to breaking an oath
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath/sworn commitment (yamin); here refers to a vow made to do or abstain from something

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking an oath when something better presents itself in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a ruling on the intersection of oath-keeping and choosing the better course of action. In Islamic jurisprudence, an oath (yamin) is a solemn binding commitment, yet this hadith teaches that when a person discovers the better course contradicts their oath, acting on the better course itself serves as the expiation (kaffara) — without the need for additional atonement. This ruling reflects the Sharia's concern for removing hardship: the believer is not spiritually penalized for choosing what is more beneficial.
